we identified new associations between the supragingival microbial community and dental caries, at the species, strain and functional levels.

the supragingival bacterial microbiota of children with caries is associated with a higher abundance of Prevotella species and a lower abundance of Leptotrichiaceae species compared with the microbiota of caries-free children.

the supragingival microbial community in children with dental caries is characterized by the presence of specific strains of several species, as well as by the presence of phages, which were not identified in the supragingivals of caries-free children, and that the supraginigival microbiome of children without caries is characterized mainly by the presence of several strains of Streptococcus, which were not found in caries-associated microbiome.

the microbiome associated to caries is complex, with a core microbiome that includes many different strains, some of which may be associated with health or disease, and with functions that may also be associated with health and disease.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the microbiome of the oral cavity is a highly dynamic system, and the interactions between the microbiome, the host and the environment are highly complex and require a systems-level approach to understand the etiology and pathogenesis of dental caries and other diseases of the oral cavity.
metagenome shotgun sequence analysis coupled with advanced analysis algorithms is a promising strategy for microbiome analysis.
